newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli-Arab violence rages on in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli-Arab violence rages on in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli troops firing rubber bullets wounded at least 22 Palestinian demonstrators armed with stones and firebombs on Saturday as unrest raged on in the volatile West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said.

In the West Bank town of Nablus, 10,000 Palestinians from rival Islamist, nationalist and leftist factions joined forces to condemn a U.S. Congressional vote calling for the recognition of Arab East Jerusalem as part of Israel's capital.
Witnesses said the Hebron unrest opened when scores of Palestinians, some masked in Arab headscarves, charged at Israeli troops on the dividing line between Israeli- and PLO-run sectors of the city.
Violence has erupted in the divided town that is home to 100,000 Arabs and 400 Jewish settlers every day for a week, wounding scores of Palestinians.

The clashes underscored tensions over a three-month impasse in Israeli-Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) peace moves sparked by Israel's ground-breaking on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
The Palestinian Authority warned in a sharply worded statement issued after a Friday night cabinet meeting that patience on the Palestinian street was wearing thin.

"The arming of Jewish settlers and the protection offered to them by Israeli soldiers while they continuously attack Palestinian landowners will not leave our masses any choice but to confront these aggressions using all available means."
The statement said Israeli settlement expansion in areas captured by the Jewish state in 1967 had spurred the unrest. Israel has accused the PLO of orchestrating the violence.

In Hebron's heart, witnesses said Israeli troops and snipers deployed across balconies, rooftops and alleyways to square off against youths armed with bottles and slingshots. Protesters burned tires, unleashing thick columns of acrid black smoke.
Witnesses said an ABC cameraman was wounded when he was struck in the head with a stone.
Emergency medical personnel treated Palestinian wounded in field hospitals. Ambulances ferried more serious casualties to Hebron's Alia hospital.

Clashes erupted in Hebron last Saturday after a U.S. congressional vote demanded President Bill Clinton recognise Arab East Jerusalem -- seen by Palestinians as the capital of their future state -- as part of Israel's capital.
In Nablus, thousands of Palestinians cheered and shouted "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest) when demonstrators burned Israeli and U.S. flags in protest against the U.S. vote.

"This decision showed the aggressive alliance between Israel and America. This shows the United States is not interested in being an honest mediator to the peace process," Nablus Governor Mahmoud al-Alloul told the rally.
Walls in the centre of self-ruled Nablus were plastered with pictures of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, assassinated Islamist bombmaker Yihya Ayyash and leftist guerrillas in exile.

Palestinian police have largely refrained from intervening in the Hebron clashes during most of the week. PLO officials have said that the Palestinian Authority was not ready to enter into a conflict with its people at a time when Israel insists on proceeding with settlement building.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to the PLO in January under a peace deal but kept troops behind to guard the heavily-fortified Jewish enclaves in the city revered by Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
